svg.text: Tuition prices, inflation and college spending
Consumer Price Index and federal education data. Sticker prices, not net of aid.
College tuition and seven other CPI series, 1979–2025
Consumer Price Index, each series set to 100 in 1979. Grey lines: the other six sectors.
The 2025 tuition & fees index is 3.3 times the all-items index.
Price rise since 1979 compared with all items
How far each sector's 2025 index sits above (or below) the all-items index.
Medical care, prescription drugs and shelter also outpaced all items; energy and gasoline did not.
Published tuition and fees at 4-year colleges, 1963–2023
Constant 2023 dollars. Public institutions and all institutions combined.
Both series have eased in real terms since their peaks; the public line is 13% below its 2015 high.
Share of core spending by function, 1987 and 2019
National share of spending by function. Institutional support is the category used here as ‘admin’.
Instruction: 48.8% to 43.1%. The three non-instruction functions shown together: 32.5% to 37.4%.
Institutional support alone moved +0.6 points. The shift is mostly academic support and student services.
• CPI tuition and published tuition are sticker prices, not net of grant aid.
• ‘Admin’ here means the IPEDS category institutional support only; its share is roughly flat (about 15%).
• Spending shares splice Delta Cost Project (1987–2012) and IPEDS (2013 on); seam at 2012.
Sources: BLS CPI-U; NCES Digest Table 330.10; NCES Delta Cost Project; IPEDS Finance. Data from public sources.
